current_law_statement: Sessions reviewed: 2024, 2025 and 2026 regular sessions via the Secretary of State's Session Laws amended/repealed tables. K.S.A. 45-219 (fees) was last amended by L. 2025, ch. 89, § 1 (HB 2134, effective July 1, 2025) — it added the actual-cost review/redaction language, the lowest-cost-staff / salary-basis / no-benefits rules, and subsection (e) (5-hour/$200 cost-mitigation contact; 3-business-day deemed withdrawal). No 2026 session law touched 45-218, 45-219 or 45-220 (2026 changes: 45-221 [ch. 100] and 45-229 [ch. 29] only). Codified statutes were available and opened on ksrevisor.gov (text current through the 2026 session, referencing K.S.A. 2025 Supp.). KORA delegates no fee figure to any regulation for local governments; state-branch fee regimes ((c)(5)-(7), (d)) and Executive Order 18-05 are recorded as agency-only. Guidance-vs-law gap: the AG's KORA FAQ/Citizen's Guide could not be opened (HTTP 403); nothing in the opened statutes, AG opinions (87-4, 93-126, 2009-14) or agency schedules supplies a municipal figure beyond the actual-cost/reasonable standard.

resolutions.source_language: Except as provided by subsection (h) or where fees for inspection or for copies of a public record are prescribed by statute, each public agency may prescribe reasonable fees for providing access to or furnishing copies of public records, subject to the following: … In the case of fees for copies of records, the fees shall not exceed the actual cost of furnishing the requested records, including the cost of staff time required to make the information available. Actual costs may include the cost to review and redact the requested records but shall not include incidental costs incurred by the public agency that are not attributable to furnishing the requested records.
resolutions.notes: No statewide per-page rate for municipalities. Standard = 'reasonable fees' capped at 'the actual cost of furnishing the requested records, including the cost of staff time'; incidental non-attributable costs excluded. The city supplies the per-page value under this ceiling. AG Op. 87-4 (1987) found a school district's 20-cents-per-page fee 'not unreasonable' because it reflected documented actual cost — a fact-specific finding, not a statewide figure. The $.25/page 'deemed reasonable' safe harbor at K.S.A. 45-240(c) applies ONLY to not-for-profit entities receiving public funds, not to public agencies. State-agency practice (NOT binding on municipalities): Dept. of Administration KORA page charges $0.25/page copies after 1 hour of staff time or 100 pages (EO 18-05, residents), staff time at rate of pay (attorney $60/hr, clerical $18/hr, IT $38/hr), mailing $0.50 first 5 pages/$0.25 per additional 5 pages, fax $0.65 per 10 pages; Secretary of State: $0.25/page paper, $0.125/page electronic, clerical $21/hr, attorney $52/hr, IT $42/hr, estimate must be prepaid, $30 returned-check fee. These are single-agency policies under K.S.A. 45-219(c)(7) ('established ... by the agency head'), not a uniform state schedule.

resolutions.source_language: In the case of fees for copies of records, the fees shall not exceed the actual cost of furnishing the requested records, including the cost of staff time required to make the information available. Actual costs may include the cost to review and redact the requested records but shall not include incidental costs incurred by the public agency that are not attributable to furnishing the requested records.
resolutions.notes: KORA does not distinguish color from B&W copies; no color-specific figure anywhere in statute, K.A.R., AG opinions or agency schedules opened. Any color rate a city sets is governed by the same actual-cost-of-furnishing ceiling. Documented absence of a color-specific figure; resolution reflects the governing standard.

resolutions.source_language: In the case of fees for copies of records, the fees shall not exceed the actual cost of furnishing the requested records, including the cost of staff time required to make the information available. Actual costs may include the cost to review and redact the requested records but shall not include incidental costs incurred by the public agency that are not attributable to furnishing the requested records. … If it is necessary to use other facilities for copying, the cost thereof shall be paid by the person desiring a copy of the records. In addition, the public agency may charge the same fee for the services rendered in supervising the copying as for furnishing copies under subsection (c) and may establish a reasonable schedule of times for making copies at other facilities.
resolutions.notes: No oversized/nonstandard-page figure in KORA. Same actual-cost ceiling governs; where copying must be done at other facilities (e.g., large-format), 45-219(b) makes the requester pay that facility cost plus the same supervision fee as for furnishing copies (KS-0040).

resolutions.source_language: In the case of fees for copies of records, the fees shall not exceed the actual cost of furnishing the requested records, including the cost of staff time required to make the information available. Actual costs may include the cost to review and redact the requested records but shall not include incidental costs incurred by the public agency that are not attributable to furnishing the requested records. … A public agency shall not be required to provide copies of radio or recording tapes or discs, video tapes or films, pictures, slides, graphics, illustrations or similar audio or visual items or devices, unless such items or devices were shown or played to a public meeting of the governing body thereof, except that the public agency shall not be required to provide such items or devices that are copyrighted by a person other than the public agency.
resolutions.notes: No specialty-reproduction schedule. Copies of photos/AV items are not required unless shown or played at a public meeting of the governing body (KS-0044); when furnished, the actual-cost ceiling applies. Transcripts by certified shorthand reporters are carved out of (c) and priced under Kansas Supreme Court rules (45-219(h)) — not a municipal fee. Other-facility copying at cost to requester (KS-0040).

resolutions.source_language: In the case of fees for copies of records, the fees shall not exceed the actual cost of furnishing the requested records, including the cost of staff time required to make the information available. Actual costs may include the cost to review and redact the requested records but shall not include incidental costs incurred by the public agency that are not attributable to furnishing the requested records. … If the public agency incurs costs for staff time to provide access to or furnish copies of public records, the agency shall use in good faith the lowest-cost category of staff reasonably necessary to provide access to or furnish copies of public records. Charges for staff time shall be based on the employee's salary or hourly wage. Charges for staff time shall not include the costs of employee benefits.
resolutions.notes: No dollar rate. Search/retrieval staff time is chargeable as part of 'the cost of staff time required to make the information available'; the rate is capped at 'the employee's salary or hourly wage', excluding benefits, and the agency must use in good faith 'the lowest-cost category of staff reasonably necessary'. City supplies actual wage-based rates. Agency-specific published rates (DoA attorney $60/clerical $18/IT $38; SOS clerical $21/attorney $52/IT $42) are those agencies' own wage-based figures, not municipal values.

resolutions.source_language: In the case of fees for copies of records, the fees shall not exceed the actual cost of furnishing the requested records, including the cost of staff time required to make the information available. Actual costs may include the cost to review and redact the requested records but shall not include incidental costs incurred by the public agency that are not attributable to furnishing the requested records. … If the public agency incurs costs for staff time to provide access to or furnish copies of public records, the agency shall use in good faith the lowest-cost category of staff reasonably necessary to provide access to or furnish copies of public records. Charges for staff time shall be based on the employee's salary or hourly wage. Charges for staff time shall not include the costs of employee benefits.
resolutions.notes: Review and redaction time is expressly chargeable ('Actual costs may include the cost to review and redact the requested records'); AG Op. 2009-14 confirms 'The cost of redaction may be assigned to the record requestor.' Rate capped at salary/hourly wage of lowest-cost reasonably necessary staff, no benefits. No dollar figure.

resolutions.source_language: In the case of fees for providing access to records maintained on computer facilities, the fees shall include only the cost of any computer services, including staff time required. … If the public agency incurs costs for staff time to provide access to or furnish copies of public records, the agency shall use in good faith the lowest-cost category of staff reasonably necessary to provide access to or furnish copies of public records. Charges for staff time shall be based on the employee's salary or hourly wage. Charges for staff time shall not include the costs of employee benefits.
resolutions.notes: For records maintained on computer facilities, fees 'shall include only the cost of any computer services, including staff time required'; staff time at salary/wage, no benefits. No dollar figure. AG Op. 93-126: an agency 'is not required to acquire or design a special program to produce information' (context: 1993 opinion to City of Lenexa).

resolutions.unit: enum (always | never | over N pages | over N hours); paper-only scope: no — applies to paper copies, access, and computer-facility records alike
resolutions.source_language: In the case of fees for copies of records, the fees shall not exceed the actual cost of furnishing the requested records, including the cost of staff time required to make the information available. Actual costs may include the cost to review and redact the requested records but shall not include incidental costs incurred by the public agency that are not attributable to furnishing the requested records. … In the case of fees for providing access to records maintained on computer facilities, the fees shall include only the cost of any computer services, including staff time required. … If the public agency incurs costs for staff time to provide access to or furnish copies of public records, the agency shall use in good faith the lowest-cost category of staff reasonably necessary to provide access to or furnish copies of public records. Charges for staff time shall be based on the employee's salary or hourly wage. Charges for staff time shall not include the costs of employee benefits.
resolutions.notes: Staff time (search, making available, review/redaction, computer services) is chargeable from the first minute — KORA sets no page or hour threshold below which labor is free, and applies to both 'providing access to' and 'furnishing copies of' records. Requirement-vs-permission: chargeability is a Permission (a city may charge less or nothing); the 5-hour/$200 figures in 45-219(e)(1) are triggers for the mandatory cost-mitigation contact, NOT a free-labor threshold. State agencies' 1-hour-free practice (DoA) is agency policy only.

resolutions.source_language: Charges for staff time shall be based on the employee's salary or hourly wage. Charges for staff time shall not include the costs of employee benefits. … In the case of fees for copies of records, the fees shall not exceed the actual cost of furnishing the requested records, including the cost of staff time required to make the information available. Actual costs may include the cost to review and redact the requested records but shall not include incidental costs incurred by the public agency that are not attributable to furnishing the requested records.
resolutions.notes: No overhead/fringe surcharge is permitted: staff-time charges 'shall not include the costs of employee benefits', and 'incidental costs ... not attributable to furnishing the requested records' are excluded. Engine value 0%. (Added by L. 2025 ch. 89.)

resolutions.source_language: If the public agency incurs costs for staff time to provide access to or furnish copies of public records, the agency shall use in good faith the lowest-cost category of staff reasonably necessary to provide access to or furnish copies of public records. Charges for staff time shall be based on the employee's salary or hourly wage. Charges for staff time shall not include the costs of employee benefits.
resolutions.notes: No statutory billing increment or rounding rule; charges must be 'based on the employee's salary or hourly wage'. Agency schedules opened (DoA, SOS) state hourly rates but no increment. resolutions.unit: hours of staff time | USD (estimated actual cost of staff time) — whichever is exceeded
resolutions.source_language: When the staff time needed to respond to a records request will exceed five hours or the estimated actual cost for staff time needed to fill the request exceeds $200, the public agency shall make reasonable efforts to contact the requester and engage in interactive communication about mitigating costs to fill the request. The requester is not obligated to mitigate costs. … Upon request, a public agency shall provide to the person requesting access to or copies of public records pursuant to this section an itemized statement of costs incurred by the public agency and charged to such requester. Such itemized statement shall include, but not be limited to, the hourly rates charged for each employee involved in making the requested records available and an itemized list of any other fees charged to provide access to or furnish copies of the requested records.
resolutions.notes: Shape differs from a classic itemized-estimate trigger: above the threshold the agency 'shall make reasonable efforts to contact the requester and engage in interactive communication about mitigating costs' ('reasonable efforts' = using the contact means the requester provided, (e)(3)); the requester need not mitigate. There is no separate statutory dollar trigger for a written estimate — an itemized statement of costs is owed 'upon request' at any amount ((c)(4), KS-0039), and advance payment may be required at any amount (KS-0043). Both thresholds are staff-time-only (not total cost).

resolutions.unit: business days (from the agency's reasonable-efforts contact under 45-219(e))
resolutions.source_language: If a public agency has made reasonable efforts to contact the requester pursuant to this section and the requester has failed to respond by the end of the third business day, the records request will be deemed to be withdrawn until a subsequent contact has been made by the requester to the public agency.
resolutions.notes: The window attaches to the cost-mitigation contact (triggered at 5 hours/$200), not to a formal estimate. Consequence is 'deemed to be withdrawn UNTIL a subsequent contact has been made by the requester' — reversible, not a permanent closure. 'Business day' defined at 45-217(b) (excludes Sat/Sun/holidays of the U.S., state, or the political subdivision).

resolutions.source_language: Upon request, a public agency shall provide to the person requesting access to or copies of public records pursuant to this section an itemized statement of costs incurred by the public agency and charged to such requester. Such itemized statement shall include, but not be limited to, the hourly rates charged for each employee involved in making the requested records available and an itemized list of any other fees charged to provide access to or furnish copies of the requested records.
resolutions.notes: No revised-estimate percentage or overrun-notice rule in KORA. Only related duty: itemized statement of costs actually incurred and charged, upon request ((c)(4)). SOS policy states it will 'promptly advise the requestor of any correction to the fee' — agency practice, not law. resolutions.value: none (no statutory threshold — advance payment may be required for any amount)
resolutions.source_language: A public agency may charge and require advance payment of a fee for providing access to or furnishing copies of public records, subject to K.S.A. 45-219. … If copies are requested, the public agency may require a written request and advance payment of the prescribed fee.
resolutions.manual_verification: Engine mapping: threshold = 0. The statute states no dollar figure; 'none' is the documented absence of a threshold, not a figure found in the text.
resolutions.notes: Advance payment 'of a fee' / 'of the prescribed fee' may be required without any minimum-amount condition. AG Op. 87-4 (citing State ex rel. Stephan v. Harder, 230 Kan. 573, Syl. ¶ 7 (1982)): 'An agency may require advance payment of the fee before copies are made.' State-agency practice (DoA, SOS) is to require the estimated fee up front.

resolutions.source_language: A public agency may charge and require advance payment of a fee for providing access to or furnishing copies of public records, subject to K.S.A. 45-219. … If copies are requested, the public agency may require a written request and advance payment of the prescribed fee.
resolutions.manual_verification: Derived reading: 'advance payment of the prescribed fee' is read as permitting up to the whole fee in advance; the statute states no percentage. Verify that no AG opinion or case caps partial deposits.
resolutions.notes: No partial-deposit cap: the statute permits advance payment of 'the prescribed fee' (the fee itself), so a city may require anything up to 100% before providing access or copies. Recorded as a ceiling because the city chooses the portion.

resolutions.value: prepay_permitted (agency may require advance payment before providing access to or furnishing copies)
resolutions.source_language: A public agency may charge and require advance payment of a fee for providing access to or furnishing copies of public records, subject to K.S.A. 45-219. … If copies are requested, the public agency may require a written request and advance payment of the prescribed fee.
resolutions.notes: Production (and even access) may be conditioned on advance payment; it is a Permission, so a city may also release before payment. Nothing in KORA requires the agency to release records before the fee is paid.

resolutions.source_language: If a public agency has made reasonable efforts to contact the requester pursuant to this section and the requester has failed to respond by the end of the third business day, the records request will be deemed to be withdrawn until a subsequent contact has been made by the requester to the public agency. … A public agency may charge and require advance payment of a fee for providing access to or furnishing copies of public records, subject to K.S.A. 45-219.
resolutions.notes: KORA has no 'withdrawn after N days of nonpayment' clock and no prior-debt prepayment rule. Shape the engine must express: (1) the agency may withhold access/copies until advance payment is made (KS-0043); (2) the only deemed-withdrawal trigger is requester silence for 3 business days after the agency's cost-mitigation contact (KS-0042), which is reversible on subsequent requester contact. Nonpayment per se is otherwise unaddressed — a city's own procedures under 45-220(a) may fill this.

resolutions.source_language: A public agency may charge and require advance payment of a fee for providing access to or furnishing copies of public records, subject to K.S.A. 45-219.
resolutions.notes: KORA states no clock effect (tolling/pause), grace period, or lapse action for an unpaid deposit. The three-business-day 'act upon' deadline (45-218(d)) is unaffected by payment status in the text; the agency may simply not furnish copies until advance payment (KS-0043). The only lapse mechanism is the 3-business-day non-response withdrawal after a cost-mitigation contact (KS-0042), which is not a payment clock. resolutions.source_language: Except as provided by subsection (h) or where fees for inspection or for copies of a public record are prescribed by statute, each public agency may prescribe reasonable fees for providing access to or furnishing copies of public records, subject to the following:
resolutions.notes: No minimum fee in KORA. Searched: K.S.A. 45-215 through 45-254 (KORA, Revisor of Statutes, current through the 2026 session — 45-218, 45-219, 45-220, 45-221, 45-230, 45-240, 45-254 opened); 2024, 2025 and 2026 Session Laws amended/repealed tables (only 45-219 [L. 2025 ch. 89, HB 2134], 45-221 and 45-229 touched); K.A.R. resolutions.source_language: In the case of fees for copies of records, the fees shall not exceed the actual cost of furnishing the requested records, including the cost of staff time required to make the information available. Actual costs may include the cost to review and redact the requested records but shall not include incidental costs incurred by the public agency that are not attributable to furnishing the requested records. … In the case of fees for providing access to records maintained on computer facilities, the fees shall include only the cost of any computer services, including staff time required.
resolutions.notes: No CD/DVD/USB figure. Media cost falls within 'the actual cost of furnishing the requested records'; for computer-facility records fees include only computer-services cost incl. staff time. 45-219(i): agency need not let the requester attach their own device (KS-0047). SOS charges $0.125/page for electronic copies — agency policy only.

resolutions.source_language: In the case of fees for copies of records, the fees shall not exceed the actual cost of furnishing the requested records, including the cost of staff time required to make the information available. Actual costs may include the cost to review and redact the requested records but shall not include incidental costs incurred by the public agency that are not attributable to furnishing the requested records. … If it is necessary to use other facilities for copying, the cost thereof shall be paid by the person desiring a copy of the records. In addition, the public agency may charge the same fee for the services rendered in supervising the copying as for furnishing copies under subsection (c) and may establish a reasonable schedule of times for making copies at other facilities.
resolutions.manual_verification: KORA does not expressly name postage/mailing; treating it as an 'actual cost of furnishing' (attributable, not incidental) is a reading of (c)(1). Confirm no AG opinion treats postage as an excluded incidental cost.
resolutions.notes: No mailing/handling/pickup/email figures. Actual-cost ceiling governs; costs of copying at other facilities are borne by the requester (KS-0040). Agency schedules (DoA/SOS mailing $0.50 first 5 pages, $0.25 per further 5 pages; express delivery arranged and paid by requester) are agency policies, not municipal law.

resolutions.source_language: Except as provided by subsection (h) or where fees for inspection or for copies of a public record are prescribed by statute, each public agency may prescribe reasonable fees for providing access to or furnishing copies of public records, subject to the following:
resolutions.notes: KORA contains no certified-copy fee. Certification fees that exist in Kansas law are officer-specific outside KORA (e.g., register of deeds fees, K.S.A. 28-115 — county officers) and are not municipal open-records fees; KS-0010 'certification' is the requester's non-commercial-use certification, a different concept. resolutions.unit: USD (reasonable fee / actual cost) — no per-recording, per-minute or free-minute figures
resolutions.source_language: A public agency shall not be required to provide copies of radio or recording tapes or discs, video tapes or films, pictures, slides, graphics, illustrations or similar audio or visual items or devices, unless such items or devices were shown or played to a public meeting of the governing body thereof, except that the public agency shall not be required to provide such items or devices that are copyrighted by a person other than the public agency. … The law enforcement agency shall allow the person to listen to the requested audio recording or to view the requested video recording within 20 days after making the request, and may charge a reasonable fee for such services provided by the law enforcement agency.
resolutions.effective_status: 45-219: Amended effective 2025-07-01 (L. 2025, ch. 89, § 1 [HB 2134]); no 2026 amendment; 45-254: Current (L. 2016 ch. 82; L. 2018 ch. 87; L. 2021 ch. 82; no 2024-2026 amendment)
resolutions.notes: Two layers: (1) copies of audio/video items are not required unless shown or played at a public meeting of the governing body (KS-0044); when furnished, the actual-cost ceiling applies. (2) Body-camera/vehicle-camera recordings are criminal investigation records; a law enforcement agency (including municipal police) must let a subject person/parent/heir/attorney listen or view within 20 days and 'may charge a reasonable fee for such services' (new row KS-9001) — a soft standard, no number.

resolutions.source_language: Except as provided by subsection (h) or where fees for inspection or for copies of a public record are prescribed by statute, each public agency may prescribe reasonable fees for providing access to or furnishing copies of public records, subject to the following: … In the case of fees for copies of records, the fees shall not exceed the actual cost of furnishing the requested records, including the cost of staff time required to make the information available. Actual costs may include the cost to review and redact the requested records but shall not include incidental costs incurred by the public agency that are not attributable to furnishing the requested records.
resolutions.notes: No commercial-purpose fee schedule or surcharge in KORA, and no definition of 'commercial purpose'. Because every fee is capped at actual cost regardless of requester and labor is already chargeable to all requesters, a purpose-based surcharge has no room under (c)(1). Kansas instead restricts commercial use of name-and-address lists (45-230) and lets the agency require a written non-commercial-use certification (45-220(c)(2), KS-0010). resolutions.notes: KORA has no fee-waiver framework (no public-interest/indigency grounds, no purpose statement, no written-denial or appeal for waiver). Whether to charge at all is discretionary under the permissive 'may prescribe reasonable fees'. Executive Order 18-05 (first 100 pages free for Kansas residents) binds only executive-branch agencies under the Governor (KS-9002). resolutions.source_language: Each request for access to a public record shall be acted upon as soon as possible, but not later than the end of the third business day following the date that the request is received. If access to the public record is not granted immediately, the custodian shall give a detailed explanation of the cause for further delay and the place and earliest time and date that the record will be available for inspection.
resolutions.notes: No provision that a late response forfeits the fee. The prior linkage to KS-0042 was wrong: 45-219(e)(2) is a REQUESTER-side non-response withdrawal, not an agency-side forfeiture. Remedies for agency non-compliance are judicial (45-222) and outside the fee engine. resolutions.source_language: The custodian may refuse to provide access to a public record, or to permit inspection, if a request places an unreasonable burden in producing public records or if the custodian has reason to believe that repeated requests are intended to disrupt other essential functions of the public agency. However, refusal under this subsection must be sustained by preponderance of the evidence.
resolutions.notes: No fee aggregation threshold or carry-forward: the 5-hour/$200 mitigation trigger applies per 'records request'. The only repeat-request rule is a non-fee refusal permission for 'repeated requests ... intended to disrupt other essential functions' (KS-0031, Denials). new_rules.legal_concept: Reasonable fee for allowing subject persons to listen to/view body-camera or vehicle-camera recordings
new_rules.atomic_rule: When a person described in K.S.A. 45-254(c) (subject of the recording, parent/guardian of a minor subject, heir at law of a deceased subject, or their attorney) requests to listen to or view a body-camera or vehicle-camera recording, the law enforcement agency shall allow it within 20 days and may charge a reasonable fee for such services.
new_rules.trigger: Request under 45-254(b) by a person listed in 45-254(c) to listen to/view a body or vehicle camera recording
new_rules.clock_spec: 20 calendar-days from making the request (viewing/listening must be allowed)
new_rules.source_language: The law enforcement agency shall allow the person to listen to the requested audio recording or to view the requested video recording within 20 days after making the request, and may charge a reasonable fee for such services provided by the law enforcement agency.
new_rules.notes: Applies to every 'law enforcement agency' — municipal police included (all_public_bodies operating law enforcement). 'Reasonable fee' is a soft standard; no per-recording/per-minute figure. The recordings are criminal investigation records (45-254(a); 45-217(e)(1)); this section grants an access right and fee permission in addition to any KORA disclosure. Copies of AV items generally are not required under 45-219(a) unless shown/played at a public meeting (KS-0044).

new_rules.legal_concept: Executive Order 18-05 — no copy charge for first 100 pages (Kansas residents, executive-branch agencies under the Governor)
new_rules.atomic_rule: Executive-branch departments, agencies, boards and commissions under the jurisdiction of the Office of the Governor shall not assess any charge or fee for copying documents responsive to a KORA request made by a Kansas resident, up to and including the first 100 pages, and shall inform resident requesters of this policy in the initial response.
new_rules.trigger: KORA request by a resident of Kansas to an executive-branch agency under the Governor
new_rules.source_language: The Office of the Governor and all Executive Branch departments, agencies, boards, and commissions under the jurisdiction of the Office of the Governor shall not assess any charge or fee for the copying of documents responsive to an open records request made by any resident of Kansas under the Kansas Open Records Act, up to and including the first one hundred (100) pages of such documents. All residents of Kansas making such a request shall be informed of this policy in the initial response to their request.
new_rules.source_authority: Kansas Executive Order No. 18-05, 'Open Records Copy Charges' (Gov. Jeff Colyer, 2018)
new_rules.effective_status: Effective immediately on filing with the Secretary of State (2018); still cited as operative on admin.ks.gov (accessed 2026-08-19) — currency requires manual verification (no rescission located)
new_rules.notes: STATE_AGENCIES_ONLY — does not bind municipalities, counties, school districts, or non-cabinet state entities. Recorded per the run parameter to note the agency regime; for municipalities the free-page item is silent. Source type: an Executive Order (not in the V2 source-type list; nearest is Official Guidance). Signing date is in the image signature block, not the PDF text layer. Opened via the Kansas Government Information Online Library (KGI, Kansas State Library) copy of the filed order.

applicability_notes: K.S.A. 45-217(k): 'public agency' means the state or any political or taxing subdivision — every 45-218/45-219 fee provision binds municipalities and state agencies alike (all_public_bodies), except (c)(5)-(7), (d) and (f), which are branch-specific to state government.

The only Kansas figures that look like a per-page copy rate ($0.25) come from (a) K.S.A. 45-240(c), a 'deemed reasonable' safe harbor for NOT-FOR-PROFIT entities receiving public funds, and (b) individual state-agency KORA policies (Dept. of Administration, Secretary of State) — neither binds a city. Web summaries that attribute '$.25 per page shall be deemed a reasonable fee' to K.S.A. 45-219 are wrong; the opened Revisor text of 45-219 contains no such clause.

Executive Order 18-05 (first 100 pages free for Kansas residents) binds only executive-branch agencies under the Governor; recorded as KS-9002 (state_agencies_only). Municipal free-page allowance is silent.
K.S.A. 45-219(d) fee-reasonableness appeal to the Secretary of Administration is limited to records 'within the executive branch'; municipal requesters have only judicial review (45-222).
K.S.A. 45-254(b) 'reasonable fee' for viewing/listening to body/vehicle camera recordings binds every law enforcement agency, including municipal police (KS-9001).

State-agency hourly rates (DoA attorney $60/clerical $18/IT $38; SOS clerical $21/attorney $52/IT $42) are those agencies' own wage-based figures under (c)(3) — illustrative of the salary/wage basis, not municipal defaults.
material_negatives: No statewide per-page copy rate, color/oversized/specialty rate, graduated bands, free-page allowance, minimum fee, or de-minimis floor for municipalities — every duplication charge sits under 'reasonable' / 'actual cost of furnishing ... including staff time' (45-219(c), (c)(1)).

No dollar labor rate, billing increment, free labor hours, or per-requestor periodic allowance; labor is chargeable from the first minute at salary/hourly wage of the lowest-cost reasonably necessary staff, benefits excluded (45-219(c)(3)).
No revised-estimate percentage, estimate validity period, overrun re-issue rule, deposit percentage cap, deposit-clock tolling, nonpayment-withdrawal clock, or electronic-payment provision in KORA.
No fee-waiver framework (no public-interest/indigency grounds, purpose statement, written waiver denial, or waiver appeal) and no fee forfeiture for late response.
No commercial-purpose surcharge or schedule; no certified-copy fee; no per-recording/per-minute AV rates; no fee aggregation or carry-forward for repeat requests.
No Kansas Administrative Regulation implements KORA fees for local governments; the statute delegates no fee figure to any rule-making body for municipalities.
